{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Time: ordered timer inputs / 2

Status: integration preview. This publication defines data and the required runtime
behavior. A package import does not install a scheduler or authorize an executable
binding. Native support is an explicit host selection. The MyOS Java adapter implements
this publication; other runtimes must qualify their own integration.

## 1. Layering and inputs

Language stores and validates Blue values. Contracts runs lifecycle handlers,
operations and workflows. BEX computes effects. This Time protocol introduces a
channel for processor-derived inputs and steps for emitting requests. Coordination
must integrate pending timers into its existing input selection, complete-prefix
publication, durable progress and account-scoped execution. No separate graph
scheduler, global ancestor barrier, per-timer Timeline, or external business entry
is introduced.

Starting management runs Contracts initialization without an incoming Timeline
entry and without an initialization timestamp. A lifecycle workflow may emit a
complete Timer Request already stored in the document. BEX does not read a clock.
An operation may also emit a request; its arrival timestamp is not used to derive
the requested deadline. A Timer Request merely stored somewhere in document data
is not active until emitted by a successful managed-document invocation.

## 2. Timestamp

The field is `timestamp`: a nonnegative Integer Unix timestamp in microseconds
since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, using the same unit as the selected Coordination
Timeline timestamps. For example, `1790931600000000` is a requested deadline, not
a measured execution time. Text dates, seconds, floating point values and booleans
are not interchangeable with this field. There is no `at`, `atUs`, `afterUs`,
implicit `now`, relative-delay base, or worker-clock field in this protocol.

The selected Contracts edition accepts external processing timestamps from 0 to
2^53 - 1 inclusive. This preview uses that existing numeric representation bound;
it does not introduce a structural, cardinality or depth limit. A different
numeric domain requires a compatible Contracts/Coordination edition and a new
Time publication, rather than silently truncating an Integer.

The processor may wake late. Once eligible, a Timer Fired input occupies the
requested deadline's logical position. Its Contracts eventTimestamp is the
request's timestamp, NOT a wall-clock observation and NOT an originating
initialization/operation timestamp. This supplies the existing three-input
Contracts interface only when the future firing is processed. Initialization
still supplies no external event or timestamp.

## 3. Messages

A Timer Request has exactly type, channel, timestamp and optionally key and
context. channel is the local Time channel key, not a Timeline ID. A supplied key
is nonempty Text. context is arbitrary valid captured Blue data, not code to
reevaluate later. Reserved metadata is interpreted under Language rules; unknown
ordinary top-level request fields are rejected by the Time runtime.

A Timer Fired has exactly type, registrationId and request. Its request is the
original committed Timer Request, preserved as an exact Blue value. An inline
presentation and a verified exact reference may differ physically without
changing that identity. No callback/workflow name is stored, and no execution
clock or inferred relative deadline is added.

A Cancel Timer Request has exactly type, channel and key. This version cancels
by key only. Cancellation by registration ID, recurrence, cron and relative
delays are outside this version. Applications may emit subsequent explicit
requests to implement their own bounded repetition.

## 4. Event effects and custom steps

Contracts/Trigger Event and BEX $appendEvent can emit a fully constructed Timer
Request. Both use normal Contracts commit/rollback behavior. A native Time/Schedule
Timer step accepts a single `request` body field, interpreted as a read-only BEX
expression. The expression returns an untyped object containing channel,
timestamp, optional key and context. The step attaches the exact Timer Request
type, validates the completed message, and returns one staged emitted event.
A result with its own type or unsupported fields is rejected, not overwritten.

Time/Cancel Timer follows the same procedure, with channel and key. Evaluating
arguments may read the current event, call, document and earlier step results
using the current Contracts expression frame. It may not read a wall clock,
perform host I/O, register a timer immediately, or reinterpret its context as
future executable code. Standard BEX gas must be charged before work, against
the same invocation budget; the step does not receive a second 10,000,000 budget.
Any effects in an expression-root evaluation are rejected.

A helper emitting the same completed request through ordinary Compute must have
the same registration meaning. Emitting a request is NOT a firing. A Triggered
Event Channel observing that request does not constitute a Time channel firing.
A conditional BEX program can choose whether to append a request. A preceding
step returning false is not implicitly a workflow branch.

## 5. Registration, scope and identities

Only effects surviving the originating document's commit create or cancel
registrations. The Time runtime must validate the entire staged effect batch
before making it eligible to commit. Malformed requests or an invalid local
channel reject the originating attempt atomically; earlier changes and requests
from that attempt do not become effective. The emitter is the managed document
that actually produced the effect, not each ancestor that later observes it.
Use Contracts provenance/effect occurrences, not a scan of public payloads.

A registration belongs to an engine/account context, managed-document identity,
Time channel key, and that channel's generation. It is not keyed by the changing
current document BlueId alone. An unrelated business update does not rearm or
invalidate it. Replacing/removing the channel or ending the managed lifetime
invalidates that generation's pending registrations. Ordinary embedding attach
or detach is not by itself removal of the separately managed child.

The canonical identity descriptor is the Blue value:

    { domain: "Time/registration/1", contextId: <stable context identity>,
      documentId: <stable managed identity>, channel: <key>,
      channelGeneration: <generation>, occurrenceId: <committed effect identity> }

registrationId is its Language BlueId. occurrenceId identifies the source commit
and local effect position using existing committed-effect provenance. It is not
just the emitted payload's content BlueId. Two identical emitted requests at
different occurrences create different unnamed timers; replaying the same
occurrence yields the same registration. Independent contexts need not share a
registration ID. They reproduce it when replaying the same identified context.

A key selects at most one pending registration within this scope. Reusing the key
replaces that pending registration with a new identity. Without a key each
occurrence is independent. Cancellation of a missing key is an idempotent no-op.
Replacement and cancellation only affect a registration they precede in logical
input order; they cannot undo an already prior firing. One source commit's
requests and cancellations apply in their emitted order. Thus schedule-then-
cancel leaves no pending timer; cancel-then-schedule leaves the new one pending.

## 6. Eligibility, completeness and deterministic order

A host alarm is only a wake-up hint. Firing requires evidence that authoritative
time has reached the requested timestamp, relevant histories are closed through
the required boundary, all predecessors/prerequisites have been processed, and
the registration is still pending. A fetched latest head or silence on an idle
Timeline is insufficient. Strictly increasing append timestamps alone do not
prove that an earlier unobserved entry cannot arrive. A completeness promise
must establish both availability of the required prefix and that future accepted
entries cannot be inserted into that closed prefix.

The required source set is the document's current dependency/history selection,
not a list frozen when the timer was first emitted and not every Timeline on the
platform. Missing authorized history means WAITING, not permission to ignore a
possible earlier cancellation. Reevaluate dependencies after earlier inputs or
topology changes. Preserve exact historical child outcomes and the existing
cyclic dependency/group rules; a new Time feature must not reintroduce a global
parent-completion barrier or deadlock a cycle by demanding impossible mutually
final completeness.

Pending timers occupy candidate positions as soon as their source commit is
visible. Every input uses Coordination's lexicographic order
(timestamp, sourceBlueId, entryBlueId). An ordinary entry uses its Timeline ID;
a timer uses its Timer Source ID and Timer Entry ID. There is no input-class
priority. At equal timestamps a cancellation wins only when its entry precedes
the timer. Dependency prerequisites still take precedence; this is not a new
global order across unrelated documents.

Each managed document has one immutable Timer Source with exactly type,
contextId and documentId (the stable managed identity, not its current state ID).
A Timer Entry has exactly type, source (an exact Timer Source reference),
timestamp (the requested deadline), and message (an exact Timer Fired reference).
Its message contains the registration identity and original request. Neither
object contains arrival time, worker identity, mutable status or a predecessor.
Multiple timers may have the same source and timestamp. Pending entries are
candidates, not append operations on a strictly increasing Signed Timeline.

The Time adapter admits this exact Timer Entry type wherever the selected
Coordination receipt/history/attachment format records the effective input.
It preserves the existing order tuple and receipt construction. This extension
is enabled only for the exact approved Time publication; arbitrary entry types
remain invalid. The outer Timer Entry is the durable input identity, whereas
Contracts receives its Timer Fired message and deadline. Retained completion
records preserve both identities so receivers verify the original invocation.
Ordinary Signed Timeline validation and its strict timestamp rule are unchanged.

A newly emitted request must have a timestamp strictly greater than the
invocation's logical timestamp, regardless of whether its cause is an operation,
a timer or a received child outcome. New child initialization inherits the
causal floor of the attaching invocation. Requests at or before that floor are
rejected as TIME_DEADLINE_BEFORE_POSITION before publication. No fixed minimum
interval is imposed beyond strict increase. Hosts may fairly throttle processing
without changing logical timestamps or skipping backlog positions. Pending
registration quotas are host resource limits, not automatic recurrence rules.

A genuinely new standalone document with no committed external position may
initialize with an already elapsed absolute deadline. Process it as due once
time and input completeness are established. A previously committed overdue
registration after downtime also retains its original candidate position; it
is not a new backdated registration.

## 7. Admission and authority

Time/Timer Channel derives from Contracts/Channel, NOT from a generic accepting
External Channel. Bind its exact type and rules identity to a trusted
external-channel implementation. This is an external input to the Contracts
machine, but it is generated by the document processor, not appended by a user
to a Timeline. Unsupported Time channels and steps must fail explicitly.
Loading the package data must never enable them automatically.

Before preparation, the runtime binds admission evidence to the exact receiver
snapshot, managed identity, channel and generation, event identity, registration,
requested timestamp, prerequisite coverage, and engine context. Recheck it on
replay. A Timer Fired-shaped payload on a Timeline, a forged client evidence
object, wrong generation, replaced key, duplicate completed registration, or
mismatched request cannot create a timer firing. Ordinary Timeline inputs can
still be observed by ordinary Timeline workflows, but never impersonate Time
channel admission. Timer firing conveys only the agreed document transition;
it cannot impersonate a party or bypass another document's operation authority.

## 8. Durable progress, parents and failure

The authoritative state is committed effects plus durable per-registration
progress. Pending wake-up indexes are reconstructible projections. Persist the
source cursor, registration identity, generation, key replacement/cancellation,
selected input and terminal disposition with idempotent writes and the engine's
existing publication/receipt protocol. Do not require cross-table PostgreSQL
transactions or treat multiple uncoordinated writes as atomic.

A crash before the source commit exposes no timer. A crash after commit but before
index update must rediscover it. Commit results and firing disposition through
the existing durable publication protocol so a crash cannot create a second
committed firing or lose the first. An old alarm after cancel/replace is harmless.
Do not mark a timer done before its outcome is durable. This publication does
not prescribe a new journal implementation in the data package.

An unresolved timer at T holds the receiver's complete-prefix publication before
its position. A parent must not be told its child is complete through T while the
child still owes a timer-driven transition there. This is a per-dependency
completeness requirement, not a rule that the child waits for all parents before
continuing. Shared parents consume the retained completed child history without
rerunning that child once per embedding.

One-shot timers become terminal after their committed processing disposition.
A successful firing with no matching workflow is terminal NO_MATCH. A deterministic
Contracts failure or gas exhaustion follows the selected Coordination terminal
input policy, with rollback and recorded disposition; it must not permanently
block later input or retry forever as though it were a missing wake-up. Host
crash, resource shortage, unavailable proofs or unfunded account are not such
terminal semantic results. Preserve account-scoped authority/access and budgets.

## 9. Metering and qualification

The Contracts 10,000,000 shared gas ceiling is unchanged. BEX evaluation, message
construction, validation and accepted effect processing must be charged through
the chosen runtime before proportional work. Candidate discovery/proof retrieval
is host work subject to host and account budgets, not an invented unbounded
free background workload. No new universal timer-count, graph-depth or collection
cardinality ceiling is introduced. Exact native tariffs, metering of admission
validation, cyclic progress, durable storage and cross-language parity must be
qualified before native support is advertised. The conformance harness's fixture
counters are not a calibrated production gas policy.

This edition selects the exact 10M gas prerequisites. Previously published content retains its original semantics.

**Status:** normative candidate rules for a local experimental publication; not a qualified release or an implemented conformance claim.
**Proposed edition:** `blue-contracts/2026-10-22-demand-scoped-1`.
**Proposed package version:** `1.0.0-demand-scoped.1`; final release metadata is assigned by the canonical build owner.
**Baseline:** [final-gas specification](contracts-final-gas.md).
**Conformance and implementation gates:** [demand-scoped cases](contracts-demand-scoped-conformance.md).

The canonical build assigns the candidate BlueIds from these exact rules and their pinned imports. Prior archived publications and existing specifications remain unchanged. This candidate may be built locally to bind and test the new implementation; it MUST NOT become a production default or a qualified release until the linked conformance gates and normal lifecycle tests pass. Sections 12.1–12.5 define the replacement algorithms and take precedence over the baseline's conflicting whole-certification and whole-closure calls; baseline scheduling and unrelated semantics remain unchanged. The candidate label is not evidence that D1–D5 have passed.

## 1. Contract and compatibility

The new edition defines successful execution as completion of every obligation required by the requested Contracts transition, including its required evidence retention. It does not certify every value transitively reachable from its input, event or result. Blue Language remains the authority for exact identity, effective types, constraints, exact evidence and cyclic proof validation. `strict_certify`/`NativeRuntime.strict` retain their full meaning.

The public cause remains the original exact event and supplied timestamp. Channel Event Checkpoint retains `event: {blueId: ORIGINAL_EVENT_ID}`. Event bytes, signatures and predecessor links MUST NOT be rewritten. This edition introduces neither `entryId` nor `eventProofs`, serialized coverage certificates, external completion tokens or new trusted claims in document content.

All prior editions retain their original processing, certification, gas and storage rules. An exact installed edition binding selects this policy before a request executes; availability, account age, author-supplied labels and cache state cannot select it. New and old account runtimes may coexist in one process without sharing edition-dependent conclusions. Cross-edition processing of one managed document is outside this release.

Unless explicitly revised here, retain the final-gas edition's operation selection, deterministic scheduling, protected markers, occurrence identities, lifecycle, generalization, failure observations and public API. Coordination determines signed source validity, authority, history and admission under its separately selected edition; Contracts does not infer these from an event-shaped value.

## 2. One obligation policy

An invocation has a private working context and an obligation set. An obligation identifies:

```
(edition, input snapshot, original cause, current exact member/view,
 contextual Recipe, processor role, operation/purpose, required coverage)
```

The tuple is a semantic identity, not a required new serialized format. Coverage denotes what was established: exact identity/evidence, effective header, contextual predicate, selected value/subtree, managed occurrence, or complete Language value/definition. These categories MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable trust levels. A contextual predicate fact is not a whole-value certificate, even when its exact BlueId equals a completely certified value in another role.

The native processor and the actual operation determine obligations. Source availability MUST NOT change their meaning. A successful full-content execution and a successful missing-unused-content execution on the same source MUST have identical observations and logical gas. A required missing record produces `NEEDS_RESOURCES`; invalid evidence produces the native validation error; unsupported semantics produces an explicit failure, never a successful filter mismatch or a false absence.

Obligations are extended by actual observations and writes. Conditional BEX evaluation adds obligations for its discriminant and selected branch under normal BEX semantics. An unselected branch does not acquire an execution obligation merely because it is reachable. Metadata and constraints may nevertheless require inspecting it. This rule does not allow the processor to ignore an already established obligation when a resource is unavailable.

There is no exemption set keyed only by BlueId. The same exact body may be opaque predecessor data and a required current operand. The latter role MUST perform its own contextual validation and demand missing content. Repeated obligations may reuse verified facts only when their complete context and coverage agree; metering follows the logical work rule, not physical reuse.

## 3. Native observations and contextual validity

The current Java interfaces provide building blocks, not a ready-made general scoped certificate:

| Operation | Actual interface | Meaning and restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact root/evidence | `NativeRuntime.identity`, `NativeRuntime.open`; `RuntimeBridge.open` | Exact record and owning proof are verified when opened. A hash/reference alone does not establish type validity. |
| Effective contextual header | `NativeRuntime.head/readHead(Recipe, runtime)` | Preserve effective type, inherited contributions, requirements and metadata. A header is not a full certificate. |
| Descendant selection | `NativeRuntime.child(Head, key)`; `RuntimeBridge.child/select` | Derive the child from the effective parent Recipe; do not replace it with a standalone reference that loses `valueType`, `itemType` or inherited requirements. |
| Contextual whole subtree | `NativeRuntime.validate(Recipe, runtime, goal)` | Validates that selected subtree using Language semantics. It may demand descendants; it is not a partial-validation flag. |
| Containing constraints | `runtime.validateConstraints(Head, root)` | Run native constraints against the actual effective head. Constraint evaluation may demand more content. This call alone does not check every metadata, type or structural obligation. |
| Native type/definition | `NativeRuntime.ancestry/subtype`, `NativeRuntime.strict(...,"definition")` where whole definition is required | Do not replace native subtype, fixed-value, specification or schema logic with string/type-name checks. |
| Scalar observation | `RuntimeBridge.project` on the selected Recipe | Projection consumes a value; its result must not be hashed as the original exact identity. |
| Full certificate | `NativeRuntime.strict` / `RuntimeBridge.certify` | Unchanged complete Language check; only actual successful full checks may populate its cache. |

Every operation that observes a node MUST establish the validity of the information it uses, including the containing constraints that govern that observation. Own and inherited type/schema, `specification`, fixed values, labels, merge policy and container metadata are not optional simply because the selected descendant is otherwise well typed. Requiredness, presence and absence are resolved through the effective parent; unavailable evidence is not absence.

A processor MAY defer a child's value validation only if neither its action nor a governing predicate requires that value. It MUST still check governing predicates that apply at its selected container boundary. For example, an invalid `maxFields` on `contracts` cannot be bypassed by validating each contract separately. A `valueType` constraint on `count` cannot be discharged by certifying the number outside its parent. A specification reference required for the selected node must resolve and validate with Language's definition semantics.

The lowering of each native handler into these obligations MUST be listed and tested. If a Language predicate requires the entire subtree, invoke that native predicate with the required evidence; do not substitute a structural guess. If the existing interfaces cannot express a necessary selected predicate without imposing unrelated full validation, record an executable reproducer and an explicit API/design decision before publication. This draft does not authorize altering Language or BEX semantics or introducing a global skip-validation switch.

### 3.1 First bounded lowering: required containers

The initial additive Java primitive observes an already-required object or list container. It does not decide optional-child presence and is not a replacement for complete snapshot validation. It verifies authored and effective type/specification/item/key/value metadata through native definition checks. For an empty effective constraint description, there is no constraint predicate to evaluate: after explicit required-container shape checks, this lowering does not call the native constraint routine's incidental concrete-child counting. A nonempty effective constraint continues through native evaluation and may widen the demand, except for the required-object presence lowering below. This is a Contracts obligation/gas-plan decision, not a change to Language strict validation.

A container/header obligation MUST retain its original contextual Recipe and discharge its governing definitions. After constructing the native effective Head and establishing presence using the existing native occurrence/root rules, it MAY discharge the effective constraint without native object-field counting if and only if the Head kind is `object`, the checked occurrence is present, and the effective constraints description contains exactly `required` with a Boolean value. The required-presence predicate is then satisfied; no field-count predicate exists. This MUST still charge the existing `schemaPredicateEvaluated` obligation for `required` and MUST NOT establish a whole-value certificate or reusable value obligation.

Absent occurrences, scalar/list/none kinds, and every other effective constraint combination MUST continue through native validation. Inherited constraints are part of the effective description. In particular, `minFields`, `maxFields`, key/value/item rules and required scalar/list payload checks MUST NOT be bypassed. Governing metadata and observed ordinary records retain their existing obligations. Native presence remains authoritative: an object-shaped definition alone is not a present value. Legacy validation and tariffs are unchanged.

Canonical key validation is currently exposed only through whole native subtree validation. The first primitive therefore widens a container with explicit `keyType` to complete selected validation; it does not claim lazy `keyType` support or duplicate Language's key parser. Actual selected-value use performs full selected exact certification plus the contextual Recipe validation, preserving parent `itemType`/`valueType` requirements. Neither the container observation nor its return value is stored as a full certificate. These restrictions remain explicit until tested lowering is expanded.

### 3.2 Handler requirements

Discovery reads the effective contract map, keys, runtime type ancestry, ordering and fields used to classify/route a declaration. It MUST NOT project or certify an entire workflow merely to identify its handler. The exact installed runtime catalogue supplies the handler policy; business document IDs and workflow IDs do not.

Before an eligible handler executes, validate its consumed declaration fields, filter and selected step under their contextual Recipes. Filters preserve native presence, refinement and constraint semantics; only proven mismatch returns false. A request schema or authorization predicate that requires a payload makes that payload required. The same applies to ordinary observers: operation routing is not an exemption from an observer's actual reads.

Initial supported handler policies MUST be derived from the actual Order, Activation and mandate primitive inventory. Adding a recognized custom runtime without a defined obligation policy MUST fail explicitly, not inherit a permissive policy. This is a runtime capability rule, not a business whitelist.

## 4. Boundary obligations

| Boundary | Mandatory obligations | Deferred content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh input | Source/exact identity; reject forged protected markers; effective managed shape, declaration discovery and initialization requirements | Unselected workflow bodies/branches except where governing constraints require them |
| Snapshot restore | Closed envelope, expected and recomputed commitment, release/bindings, exact member roots and cyclic ownership, root/edge/lifetime/serial/marker integrity, contextual structural constraints | Unused ordinary descendants and historical event operands; no blanket full-body fact |
| Event ingress | Original exact event identity, supplied timestamp, contextual fields needed by dispatch and applicable constraints; signed admission remains host responsibility | Predecessor payload/foreign operand content not required by this action |
| Channel/checkpoint | Native marker type and applicable contextual constraints, channel lifetime, exact event reference, timestamp scalar/range and native channel progression rules | Reachable history not consumed by these checks |
| Handler/BEX | Selected declaration/step, current read operands, native filter and required parameter constraints, captured view/resolver and logical meter | Unselected branch bodies and untouched value descendants |
| Patch | Native construction, selected path and target context, protected-state/generalization rules, constraints affected by the write, reconciled graph/occurrences | Unchanged subtrees only where their governing obligations are unaffected |
| Finalization | All outstanding local/graph obligations, stable identities and cyclic proofs, sealed source state, pending reactions and required retention | No obligation may be silently dropped at this boundary |
| Completion/receive | Local verified origin, before/after views, cause, edition/bindings, complete execution-unit membership, tickets and exact predecessor compatibility | No assumption of whole-value certification from a valid completion |
| Export/cold restore | Exact retained records and owning proofs sufficient to reconstruct the specified restore/receive obligations; expected commitments | Optional unused closure must not leak through inline ancestors |

A patch changing a type, schema, specification, container structure or managed declaration invalidates dependent obligations. Re-evaluate them on the new contextual view before the next step observes it. Do not reuse the unchanged child BlueId's old contextual result when its parent requirements changed. The existing native generalization and constraint rules remain authoritative; preservation of their effects must be demonstrated rather than replaced by post-hoc acceptance.

Identity-only observation must remain identity-only even for an inline body. Real scalar/subtree access must perform the same contextual work for inline and referenced forms. Reading a checkpoint timestamp through native projection is legitimate; rewriting its persisted representation or relaxing integer checks is not.

## 5. Invocation and publication algorithm

The following pseudocode specifies ordering and invariants. `require_for` is a proposed internal obligation operation, not an existing Language API. Its handler-specific lowering and the complete executable reference implementation are release gates.

```
execute(edition, input, originalEvent, time):
    assert installed exact edition/bindings
    tx := fork input state, Language evidence context, obligation facts,
               archive updates, completion registrations and retained output
    require_for(tx, RESTORE_OR_INPUT, input)
    require_for(tx, EVENT_DISPATCH, originalEvent, time)
    run existing deterministic Contracts scheduling in tx
        before each observation: require_for(tx, selected contextual role)
        before installing each patch: native construct/generalize and
            require_for(tx, affected contextual write obligations)
        after patch: reconcile and finalize required local/graph obligations
    require_for(tx, FINALIZE, resulting managed graph)
    retained := prepare_required_records(tx, input, result, originalEvent)
    verify retained records can satisfy cold restore and local receive obligations
    seal outcome and its cause/edition/member bindings
    atomically install tx context, stable state, retained output, archive and
        process-local completion establishment
    return APPLIED
on missing, invalid, exhausted or incomplete execution/required retention:
    discard tx effects, evidence additions, selected facts and registrations
```

This local atomic boundary is distinct from durable host publication. The host's existing journal transaction MUST atomically publish the completed state/evidence, original cause, progress, emitted effects and retry obligations. ## 6. Completion guarantee and normal receiving

A new-edition completion establishes: this installed edition executed the identified input and original cause through all required obligations, obtained the exact resulting managed state and ordered output, and prepared all evidence required by this completion's storage/receive contract. It does NOT assert complete Language validity of every transitively reachable value.

Preserve the existing local capability boundary:

1. Only the actual successful local attempt may establish an outcome; bind input snapshot identity, event BlueId/timestamp, release, exact runtime bindings, before/after member views, receipt, units and ordered effects.
2. `capture` requires that established local outcome and matching process-local provenance. Validate selected members, owner birth rules and complete unit inclusion. A user-provided receipt, after-body or matching hash is insufficient.
3. `receive`/live receive verifies issuer, capability lifetime, cause, compatible exact edition/bindings, owned members, captured occurrence tickets and predecessor views. It validates its own contextual obligations. Incorporation is not full certification of the source's opaque closure.
4. Process restart does not deserialize a trusted capability from input bytes. The installed privileged local `CompletionReader` may recover an atomically committed local completion, verify descriptor/receipt and bindings, restore required before/after evidence under this edition, and re-establish local provenance. Arbitrary imported snapshots cannot invoke this path.
5. Modified, foreign, expired, overlapping or incompatible completion records remain rejected. This edition does not define public third-party execution proofs.

The existing descriptor's `release`, `runtimes`, before/after vectors, event, timestamp and receipt carry these bindings; there is no new user-authored coverage flag. Changing an edition changes its immutable specification identity and therefore its interpretation. The reference implementation MUST explicitly apply the new guarantee at establishment and rehydration; deleting `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION` is not an implementation.

## 7. Retention, privacy and cyclic exact content

Compute required records from the obligation roles and replay/restore requirements, not from whatever extra content happens to be cached. A record may be required in one role even if another role defers the same BlueId. Retaining unused private bodies because they were available in the full-control runtime violates deterministic scoped export/privacy.

For acyclic exact records, preserve exact identity while emitting finite child references; verify identity after serialization. Traversal follows the required roles. Do not serialize an inline ancestor wholesale when it contains an excluded descendant. A missing excluded descendant is not replaced by null, empty content or a fabricated value.

For a cyclic member, retain and verify the Language owning-set proof and required member body using the existing canonical proof/body mechanism. Do not emit an ordinary acyclic `mode: exact` record under `master#i`. Deduplicate with a finite identity/context/role work set, not by dropping owning proofs or globally whitelisting an identity. Historical graph edges such as A(T) → B(T) → A(T−1) remain exact historical edges, not latest-state aliases.

Cold restore opens and verifies actual supplied exact records and owning proofs, then derives the required obligations anew under the selected edition. Serialized statements of prior validation are not trusted. Missing content needed for these obligations must still wait/fail. Record presence or prior selective success cannot seed complete closure caches, `RuntimeBridge.certified`, or full Language validation caches.

The primitive inventory must identify actual cycles used by Order/Activation. There is no global cycle prohibition. If a required cycle cannot be retained privately with valid owning evidence, report that concrete case and resolve its contract before claiming qualification.

## 8. Logical work

Preserve the existing logical tariff operations and deterministic ordering where applicable. The new edition charges the logical observations and validations defined by its obligation plan, independently of fetch count, cache warmth, inline/reference encoding and retry timing. Reusing evidence does not erase a required charge. A selected obligation ledger is not a full-certificate cache.

The old edition's all-descendant `LogicalWork.visit` cannot automatically be the new policy's walk: it may traverse deliberately unselected data. Before release, specify the traversal for each handler's obligation and its deduplication context in the executable metering appendix. Record any intentional new-edition gas difference; old A/B gas remains exact. Experimental values 569, 645 and 708 are measured comparisons for old bindings inside the overlay, not golden totals for the new publication.

## 9. Coordination interface and unresolved release gates

Contracts accepts the original cause and supplied time. Coordination is responsible for signed prefix verification, authority, receiver history, Q06 routing, Q13 catch-up and durable scheduling. Skipping an unrelated operation is not a synthetic Contracts checkpoint. An ordinary observer can independently require event content. No new global `unknown => NO_MATCH` rule is introduced here.

The companion [receiver-relative replay draft](../../blue-coordination/spec/receiver-relative-replay-draft.md) requires child-only historical catch-up from its original raw source and own initialization, including the birth cause, without reseeding the creating parent. Contracts must preserve exact occurrence generations, source member provenance and complete execution-unit boundaries when receiving those results. Equal standalone/embedded document state does not authorize adopting a completion from a different member origin. The caller must supply the original admitted event and frozen history context; no artificial event wrapper or fabricated checkpoint substitutes for them. Concrete owner/subgraph eligibility and same-order dependency-cycle handling require the agreed executable Coordination/Contracts composition before qualification.

The following are explicit open implementation/specification gates, not permissions to weaken checks:

- **D5 Coordination agreement:** finalize recipient/history/birth rules with the new Coordination specification. Contracts laziness alone does not solve unknown nonexact targets or raw-child history equality.

## 12. Source-based implementation algorithms for the next vertical slice

This section makes D2–D4 implementable without treating pseudocode identifiers as existing APIs. These algorithms are the proposed new-edition behavior. They remain subject to executable reference/Java equivalence tests; old-edition branches retain their current algorithms.

### 12.1 Restoration and event preparation

```
restore_required(package, expected, installedPolicy):
    check closed package/snapshot metadata and expected/recomputed commitment
    check exact release and supported runtime binding vector
    fork Language context; stage package.content in that fork
    construct member/edge metadata using existing ContractStorage.restore parsing
```

This does not invoke or populate the old `restore-body` fact. Edge identity checks in `ContractGraph.verifyEdges` remain, but the new branch invokes the declared structural obligations instead of unconditional whole `blue.certify(d.body)`. A direct selected child MUST NOT bypass ancestor-container checks: selection retains the ancestor chain/role, and the policy checks each required container before consuming the child's contextual Recipe. A child Recipe carries its value requirements, not every ancestor's cardinality predicate.

Event preparation opens the original exact event and invokes the dispatcher obligation rather than `RuntimeBridge.node(... certify=true)` on its entire history. `ContractChannels.recognize` and effective operation/filter discovery consume their declared fields. Before using any actual operand they invoke the contextual value obligation. Unknown ordinary event types are not silently marked valid: their applicable metadata and each consuming observer/filter determine native obligations. Signed proof validation stays in Coordination.

Checkpoint validation consumes type/entries/channel/timestamp/event identity under their ancestor constraints. The native timestamp projection is used for referenced and inline scalar representations alike. An event identity stored in a checkpoint does not obligate traversal of its predecessor payload. A later read through that same Ref does.

Transport preparation also retains ordinary records for local-free exact Values actually constructed during this invocation and the required evidence of its actual emitted outputs. These records use the same native shallow-record/owning-proof preparation as other required transport. Preparing exact evidence for actual emitted outputs does not add a second logical tariff or a new completion authority. The required-record worklist is not a snapshot of all available resolver evidence and not a full Language closure walk. Each role defines which child edges are required; actual consumed values and governing definitions include their required validation dependencies. A bare original event reference remains present without forcing unused payload edges.

```
prepare_records(roots, obligation roles):
    todo := deterministic required roots/roles

    check := fresh NativeRuntime with ONLY records plus explicitly declared public package records
    verify/open all prospective records in check using native evidence verification
```

### 12.5 Logical obligation traversal and reuse

This edition introduces a separate obligation ledger; it does not change the old edition's `LogicalWork.validate/visit` algorithm or select behavior by broadening `finalGas()`. One attempt owns the ledger and meter. A chunk continuation copies both; an independent attempt or cold processor starts a new ledger. Failed fork work cannot publish facts or completion, even when its returned diagnostic reports gas already consumed.

The ledger key is `(contextual Recipe.key, obligation kind, coverage)`. Kinds are `container`, `definition`, and `value`; coverage identifies the complete selected contextual subtree for `value`, and the observed container/predicate/header set for `container`. Ancestor observations have their own keys. An unchanged BlueId under a different Recipe or coverage is a distinct obligation. Container/definition success never establishes a value key. Global Language/bridge caches do not affect this logical ledger.

The reference algorithm is:

```text
require(obligation):
    first require each enclosing container in outermost-to-innermost order
    if this exact obligation key succeeded in this invocation:
        charge validationProofReused once
        return its previously established obligation result
    dispatch by kind using the algorithms below
    record success only after the native check succeeds
```

For `container`, open each authored Recipe part through `LogicalWork.open` (which charges `nodeManifestOpened` once per exact ID per invocation), construct the unchanged native effective Head, and follow its applicable governing definitions with `definition` obligations. Each type edge followed charges `typeEdgeFollowed`; each explicitly selected ordinary child edge charges `objectMemberRead`, or `listItemRead` for an index. Charge `schemaPredicateEvaluated` once for each key of the effective constraints' `describe()` map, in sorted-key order. Perform the native required-container check and native effective predicate evaluation, subject only to the required-object presence lowering in §3.1: an effective object occurrence established present by native rules, with exactly the Boolean `required` constraint, discharges that predicate without incidental field counting while retaining its predicate charge. Empty effective constraints have zero predicate charges and no concrete-count walk. Incidental resolver/cache work inside the native predicate implementation is physical work, not a second logical traversal or a whole-subtree value charge. Predicate-driven widening invokes an explicit `value` obligation, whose own charges are separate; it cannot silently establish a value certificate from the container result.

For `definition`, traverse the exact definition evidence needed by native definition certification in deterministic native field/list order. Each distinct exact manifest opened is charged through the same invocation `LogicalWork.open`. Traversed ordinary fields charge `objectMemberRead`; items charge `listItemRead`; type edges charge `typeEdgeFollowed`. Deduplicate exact cycles within this definition traversal; do not regard a cycle visit as successful native certification. Then certify with goal `definition`. Do not evaluate a definition's declared minimum, maximum, enumeration or required-value constraints against the definition as if it were a value. Owning proofs use the native evidence verifier. Only successful native definition certification establishes this definition obligation.

For `value`, use an edition-specific traversal retaining the existing `LogicalWork.visit` scalar/list/object predicate accounting on the selected contextual Recipe, including its comparisons, text blocks, integer limbs, member examinations and pending value-proof keys. The old `carriedRoots` early return is disabled: a captured/portable source identity alone is not successful contextual value coverage. The old `previous` equality shortcut is likewise disabled unless the corresponding same-invocation contextual value obligation already succeeded. Do not call the old unmodified `visit` as the new reference algorithm. Its traversal is rooted at the selected Recipe, not the surrounding document. Then require both native strict selected evidence and `NativeRuntime.validate(selectedRecipe, context, "value")`. Publish the logical pending proof keys only after both checks succeed. A prior container or definition obligation does not enter that value-proof set. Do not pass an enclosing whole-root `previous` value to skip a changed contextual requirement; unchanged-subtree reuse requires the same contextual Recipe key and previously successful value coverage in this invocation.

In the new edition, establishing the identity of an explicit `Exact.Ref` reuses that reference's exact identifier. This identity-only case returns `local=false` and MUST NOT open the referenced body, rebuild it or charge identity hashing for that body, including when the reference appears as a part of local identity construction. It MUST NOT establish an `established` fact, a value certificate or successful contextual value coverage. Constructed local values retain their existing native identity construction and hash charges. A later required value read or owning-proof verification still establishes its own native obligations; an explicit reference is not evidence of its target's validity. This clarification does not alter legacy edition tariffs.

Handler ordering, BEX execution, patch construction/generalization, graph construction, emitted-event accounting and semantic exact identity construction retain their existing tariff operations. Replace only calls whose old purpose was whole-root validation with the declared obligation algorithm. Record preparation/serialization and fresh transport verification do not add independent semantic gas; exact identity construction already charged by the semantic operation is not charged again because an exporter chooses a different equivalent record encoding. No charge depends on whether a deferred child happens to be locally available.

Post-mutation checks observe enclosing containers afresh if their contextual Recipe changed, validate the changed value in its resulting context, and recheck native structural/lifetime invariants before finalization. A failed required read, predicate, record preparation or capability prerequisite leaves the input snapshot, prior prepared package, archive and completion registry unpublished. Snapshot wire identity and original event references are never rewritten to encode obligation state.

Qualification MUST compare full/missing and warm/cold logical results for these rules, including a single exact ID read in two different contextual Recipes, container-then-value aliasing, chunk continuation and failed-attempt retry. These are new-edition tariffs; old edition golden gas and receipts remain unchanged.

The next normal-path qualification is: restore a supported managed graph, execute the existing native counter/typed/workflow primitives, establish normal completion, capture and receive it, export, open a fresh processor and perform the next operation. Required-resource rollback and malformed/cyclic evidence are separate negative cases.
